mainEntity.name: What are the main app monetization models in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: Four models cover most apps: subscription (recurring fee for ongoing value), freemium with in-app purchases (free core, paid upgrades), advertising (free app, attention monetized), and commission or transaction fees (a cut of marketplace or service transactions). Many successful apps combine two, such as freemium with a subscription tier.

mainEntity.name: Which monetization model earns the most?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on usage shape, not on the model itself. Subscriptions win for products with recurring value and retention; ads only work at large scale of daily engaged users; commissions scale with transaction volume in marketplaces; in-app purchases suit apps with strong engagement peaks. The explorer in this article lets you run your own numbers per model.

mainEntity.name: What cut do Apple and Google take from app revenue?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both stores take a commission on in-app digital purchases and subscriptions — historically 30%, reduced to 15% for most small businesses under their small-business programs and for long-running subscriptions, with ongoing regulatory changes opening alternative billing in some regions. Physical goods and many service transactions billed outside in-app purchase are not subject to the store cut.

mainEntity.name: When should an app use ads versus subscriptions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ads need scale: revenue is effectively impressions times eCPM, so small audiences earn little. If your app has a modest but engaged audience that gets recurring value, a subscription usually earns more per user by orders of magnitude. Ads fit broad, high-frequency consumer apps; subscriptions fit depth and retention.
